messages:
support-anna: P0 incoming — multiple hosted customers reporting 503s across the same model endpoint since ~09:05 UTC. Customers see 500/503 on generation requests, errors look like upstream worker failures. Raising to incidents channel. @devon-oncall can you take?

devon-oncall: On it. Any correlation IDs or example requests? Which model/version?

support-anna: Sent examples privately: customer A (req id c4a3f), customer B (req id c4a7b). Model: rw-instruct-13b-v2 pinned at v2026-03-10 on hosted-prod. Errors show "upstream worker closed connection". Latency spikes first then 503s. Customer impact: interactive chat timeouts.

devon-oncall: Pulling logs now. tagging @kevin-mlinfra — I see a surge of worker restarts on node gpu-45 around 09:03-09:07. Kernel logs show a GPU fault.

kevin-mlinfra: Can you paste the node dmesg / container logs? Also are we seeing OOMs or segfaults from the runtime?

devon-oncall: Pasting snippet (sanitized):

```
May 11 09:04:12 gpu-45 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
May 11 09:04:12 gpu-45 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
May 11 09:04:12 gpu-45 dockerd[1234]: container infer-worker-7d9 exited with code 139 (segfault)
May 11 09:04:12 gpu-45 systemd[1]: infer-worker-7d9.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=139/ENOMEM
```

kevin-mlinfra: That looks like a GPU driver fault (Xid 79) followed by evictions / segfault. Also seeing ENOMEM from cgroup OOM killer for the worker process. Could be either GPU OOM due to KV cache growth or a driver regression. Any recent runtime/image changes?

ingrid-platform: Noted — we rolled a runtime image (inference-runtime:2026-05-09) last night to address perf regressions. Also changed the default batching policy for that model to batch_size=256 -> 512 last deploy.

ryan-support: Customer reports that they increased context size on some requests (long prompts + embeddings). Could that increase KV cache footprint?

kevin-mlinfra: Yes. Larger context + higher batch sizes will blow up GPU mem. Check nvidia-smi for memory usage before crash.

devon-oncall: nvidia-smi output from gpu-45 09:02:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name       Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-40GB    On           | 0000:3b:00.0     Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory Usage               |
| 14567  C      infer-worker                    38912MiB / 40536MiB           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

kevin-mlinfra: So worker was near full memory. If batch size was effectively doubled, plus KV cache from long prompts, it could trigger OOM then driver Xid and segfault. Also need to check whether quantization/kv-cache change merged in runtime.

ingrid-platform: I can roll back the runtime image immediately to inference-runtime:2026-04-30 which doesn't have the batch policy change. Do we want a rollback or to drain that node?

devon-oncall: Short term: drain gpu-45 and take it out of rotation to stop further evictions. Medium term: rollback the runtime image and revert batching change. Also reduce default batch_size for the model to previous value.

ryan-support: I'll notify impacted customers and update status page: "Intermittent 503/500 errors for some hosted endpoints — mitigation in progress".

deploy-bot: rollback started: inference-runtime -> inference-runtime:2026-04-30 by ingrid-platform (rollback id rb-20260511-001).

monitoring-bot: Alert suppressed (grouped) — 18 alerts suppressed for gpu-45.

kevin-mlinfra: While rollback in progress, can we add a protective guard at the gateway: max_request_tokens=2048 and reject requests that exceed a token threshold for pinned models on hosted tier? That reduces risk while we stabilize.

ingrid-platform: Implemented gateway denylist rule for the model at 09:22 UTC (rule id gw-20260511-09). Requests over 2048 tokens now rejected with 413.

devon-oncall: After rollback we still saw a couple of late restarts on other nodes. Looking at commit history: a separate change to the KV cache eviction logic was merged 48h ago (PR #4126) into runtime image — that may be relevant. Kevin, can you run a repro with long prompt + high batch against a staging A100?

kevin-mlinfra: Spun up a replica, repro script:
```
# repro.sh
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api/redwood/infer \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-13b-v2","inputs":"<very long prompt...>","max_tokens":512}' &
done
```
Running now. Memory climbs linearly, hits 40GB, driver Xid 79, container segfaults. Confirmed.

ryan-support: Customer-facing note: added a temporary "Do Not Use" recommendation for the model for production traffic while we finish investigating.

devon-oncall: Root cause hypothesis: combined changes (batch_size bump + KV eviction regression + customers using longer prompts) pushed A100 memory beyond safe threshold, triggering GPU driver fault (Xid 79) and worker segfaults/evictions.

ingrid-platform: Rollback completed at 09:40 UTC. Drained gpu-45 and reimaged it. Policy reverted: batch_size back to 256. kv-cache PR reverted in runtime image.

deploy-bot: deployment rb-20260511-001 completed. Canary checks: 10/10 successful.

monitoring-bot: Errors decreased to baseline at 09:46 UTC.

support-anna: Customers A/B reported recovery at ~09:48 and confirmed latency normalized. Marking impacted customers and sending follow-up.

kevin-mlinfra: Postmortem action items:
- Reproduce automated test for large prompt + high batch to catch memory blow-up (assign kevin).
- Add guardrails in runtime to enforce soft memory cap per worker (assign kevin/ingrid).
- Add a canary policy that runs heavy-client scenarios for 24h after image changes (assign ingrid).
- Improve telemetry: track KV cache growth per request and instrument token->GPU-mem mapping (assign devex/kevin).

devon-oncall: Also add customers to an "early warning" list if they exceed expected token usage for a pinned model; support to contact them proactively.

ryan-support: I'll draft post-incident customer email and publish a status page update.

support-anna: Thanks team. Moving to postmortem channel once this thread is closed. :white_check_mark:
